thread:
Sam L: Heads-up — onboarding call with Frontera Health POC tomorrow. They want Private deployment behind their TGW and PrivateLink into our control plane. Need quick checklist for network + security Qs.
Priya M: Nice. Do they insist on preserving client source IP to the model servers? Or ok with proxy NAT?
Carlos R: They said regulatory audit requires source IP preservation for traceability. Prefer no SNAT if possible.
Nina K: That implies we need an edge proxy that forwards original IP (X-Forwarded-For) or use TCP passthrough. For PrivateLink, source-IP preservation is tricky — interface endpoints will NAT to endpoint ENIs.
Sam L: Can you summarize options / one-liner recommendation I can give them in the call?
Carlos R: Options: 1) Transit VPC with proxy fleet + preserve via proxy header (easiest); 2) Bring-your-own-proxy (BYO) inside their VPC that forwards real IPs to our Private deployment (requires ELB/NLB preserves src ip); 3) Raw L4 tunnel (GRE/DTLS) to our onprem edge (complex). Recommend option 1 or 2.
Priya M: Also need the concrete firewall allowlist — security will ask for CIDRs/ports. What's the minimal set?
NetOps: Minimal egress for control plane + telemetry + model pulls: TCP 443 outbound to our control plane IPs (we'll provide ranges). For TLS handshake and downloads. Health checks: TCP 8080 (optional) if they enable health endpoint. SSH/22 only for approved jumpbox and explicit time windows.
Sam L: Customer also asked about DNS — they want all model requests to resolve to private endpoints (no public DNS leaks).
Nina K: Recommend AWS Route 53 inbound/outbound/resolver rulesets + conditional forwarding to our VPC resolver IPs. If they use PrivateLink interface endpoints for the control plane, they should create private hosted zones or forward to our resolver. Example: set outbound resolver rule for "api.redwood.example" -> 10.10.2.5 (our resolver in their account).
Carlos R: Quick snippet to show in call:

```
# SG egress (example)
Allow TCP 443 to 203.0.113.0/24
Allow TCP 443 to 198.51.100.0/24  # model pulls
Allow UDP 123 to 0.0.0.0/0        # NTP
```

Sam L: Can we give them a sample security questionnaire answer for "Do you support PrivateLink?"
Priya M: Yes — short answer: "Yes — we support AWS Interface VPC Endpoints (PrivateLink). We can run a private control plane endpoint in your account via PrivateLink and provide per-tenant ENIs. Configuration guide and SG/CIDR requirements will be supplied during handoff."
NetOps: Add: "For preservation of client source IPs, we recommend deploying an NLB with Proxy Protocol v2 or an application proxy that forwards X-Forwarded-For headers. Interface endpoints themselves will not always preserve the original NATed source IP when traffic crosses accounts."
Sam L: Pricing question — will PrivateLink or Dedicated capacity add extra monthly fees? Customer expects breakout.
Priya M: PrivateLink setup has an onboarding engineering fee + per-endpoint monthly cost. Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) is separate — we'll provide a quote based on throughput and model mix. I'll attach ranges after call.
Carlos R: Also: ask them if their firewall team needs ICMP for MTU/PMTU discovery between spokes and our edge. Some onprem appliances block ICMP and then clients see truncation. If they block, we recommend path MTU tuning or allow ICMP type 3.
Sam L: Can we drop a short troubleshooting command for DNS check for them?
Nina K: Sure — paste this in call notes:

```
# from their VPC
dig +short api.redwood-internal.example @10.10.2.5
curl -v https://api.redwood-internal.example/status --resolve api.redwood-internal.example:443:10.10.2.6
```

Sam L: Great. Anything else for audit/compliance?
Priya M: Add KMS integration note: they can provision key via their KMS and we can integrate for at-rest encryption in Private deployments. Also mention CloudTrail logs (we can push or they can pull).
NetOps: Final ask — I'll need their allowed egress windows and point-of-contact for firewall rule change (name + ticketing). Also confirm whether they prefer SGs per subnet or centralized NAT egress.
Sam L: OK I'll capture: recommendation summary + SG snippet + DNS checks + pricing note + POC handoff doc. I'll post after the meeting.
deploy-bot: POC checklist created: https://redwood.internal/poc-checklists/frontera-1803334444 — assigned to @Sam L and @Priya M :white_check_mark:
Carlos R: Thanks — I'll be on the call for the network deep-dive.
Sam L: Perfect — see you. :thumbsup:
